How to Crochet a Star Stitch Granny Square-Free Pattern

Jump to Pattern
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 9:04
Instaread

Let’s move to this star stitch granny square, every single stitch looks like a little star sparkling.

Technically, the star stitch is similar to a single crochet decrease; both pull up multiple loops and close them at once. But while sc2tog uses just two stitches to make one, the star stitch pulls up five or six loops from different spots before finishing.

Making this square is all about a two-round repeat. I start with a simple magic loop and then alternate between a row of star stitches and a row of half double crochets. Don’t forget to turn the work every time so the stars stay puffy and clear.

I also found that working two hdc into the eye of each star makes the texture pop. This pattern is my top choice for making a cozy baby blanket or a cute summer top.

Crochet Star Stitch Granny Square – Video Tutorial

This little star stitch square looks fancy, but it’s so relaxing to make. Let’s stitch one together!

Materials

  • Yarn of Your Choice. The sample is made with wool yarn and a 3.00 mm hook. The finished granny square measures approximately 4.72 × 4.72 inches
  • Crochet Hook
  • Darning Needle
  • Scissors

Abbreviations (US Term)

  1. ch- chain stitch
  2. hdc- half double crochet
  3. dc- double crochet
  4. ch-sp- chain space
  5. slst– slip stitch for joining to a different round
  6. st– stitch
  7. inc- increase
  8. FL- front loop
  9. TL- third loop
  10. yo- yarn over

What is the Star Stitch

The star stitch is a textured crochet technique that creates a thick, cozy fabric. It’s formed by pulling up multiple loops from different points and securing them together, which creates a “star” pattern that radiates across the surface.

Step-by-Step

Round 1-Foundation round

Magic loop, ch3 (count as 1dc), 3dc, ch3; [4dc, ch3] repeat 3 times. Omit the final ch3, instead, work ch1, then 1hdc into the top of the first ch3 to join, so we can keep our hook in the ch-sp. Round 1 finished.

Round 2-First start stitch round

Starting chain space

Ch2 (count as 1hdc), 1hdc in the same ch-sp, ch1.

The first star stitch-Steps 1 to 2

Let’s begin our first star stitch.
Step 1: Insert hook into the third loop of the ch1 (marked with needle), yo, and pull up a loop (2 loops on hook).
Step 2: Insert hook into the left-side loop of the last hdc post, yo, and pull up a loop (3 loops on hook).

The first star stitch-Steps 3 to 7

Step 3: Insert hook into the current ch-sp, yo, and pull up a loop (4 loops on hook).
Step 4: Insert your hook into the next stitch, yo, and pull up a loop (5 loops on hook).
Step 5: Insert your hook into the following stitch, yo, and pull up a loop from each (6 loops on hook).
Step 6: Yo and pull through all 6 loops.
Step 7: ch1 to close the star stitch.
Now, you have finished one star stitch.

The second star stitch

To make the second star stitch, pull up a loop from each of these five locations:
The previous ch-1 sp, the left-side loop of the last star st, the last st used, and the next two stitches separately.
With 6 loops on your hook, yo and pull through all, then ch1 to close.

The next chain space

Now, we have used up all stitches on this edge and reached the next ch-sp; work 2hdc + ch3 in this ch-sp.

Complete this round

[work 2hdc in the same ch-sp, ch1. Work 2 star stitches across the side as described above. 2hdc+ch3 in the next ch-sp] repeat 3 times.
To Finish: Omit the final ch3. Instead, work ch1, then 1hdc into the top of the initial ch2 to join. This keeps your hook in the ch-sp for the next round. Round 2 finished.

Round 3-Half double crochet round

Turn over. Ch2 (count as the first hdc), 1hdc in the same ch-sp. Work hdc inc into the eye of each star stitch around, 2hdc+ch3+2hdc in each ch-sp as you go. When you return to the starting ch-sp, work 2hdc, ch1, and 1hdc into the top of the initial ch2 to join.
The Eye of the Star: The “eye” is the small hole created by the ch1 that closed the star stitch. In the second picture, the needle marks exactly where to insert your hook to work your hdc inc.

Round 4-7

From Round 4, the pattern alternates between a Star Round and an Hdc Round. Each new Star Round increases the count by 2 stars per side. Remember to turn your work before every round.

General Patterns

  • Star Round: Turn work. Work [ch2, 1hdc, ch1] in the starting ch-sp, then work star stitches across: the first star follows the “First Star” instructions; all others follow the “Second Star” instructions.
  • Hdc Round: Turn work. Work [ch2, 1hdc] in the start ch-sp, hdc inc into the eye of each star stitch.

Round 4 (Star Round): Work 4 stars per side. Corner: (2hdc, ch3, 2hdc, ch1). Join with ch1, 1hdc into the top of the first ch2.
Round 5 (Hdc Round): Work hdc inc in each eye. Corner: (2hdc, ch3, 2hdc). Join as above.
Round 6 (Star Round): Work 6 stars per side. Corner/Join as Round 4.
Round 7 (Hdc Round): Work hdc inc in each eye. To Finish: Work 2hdc, ch3 in the final corner, then slst to the top of the first ch2. Fasten off. Turn over to show the star side, and that’s your star stitch granny square.

Expanding Your Square

To make your square larger, continue alternating the Star Round and Hdc Round. Each new Star Round will add 2 stars per side. Always turn your work before each round.

Star Stitch Granny Square-Printable Pattern

This elegant granny square features a textured star stitch design, creating a dense appearance with radiating "rays".
Print Pattern Pin Pattern

Materials
  

  • Yarn of Your Choice , the sample is made with wool yarn
  • Crochet Hook , we used a 3.00 mm hook
  • Darning Needle
  • Scissors

Instructions
 

Round 1-Foundation round

  • Magic loop, ch3 (count as 1dc), 3dc, ch3; [4dc, ch3] repeat 3 times. Omit the final ch3, instead, work ch1, then 1hdc into the top of the first ch3 to join, so we can keep our hook in the ch-sp.

Round 2-First start stitch round

  • Starting chain space
    Ch2 (count as 1hdc), 1hdc in the same ch-sp, ch1.
    Let’s begin our first star stitch.
    Step 1: Insert hook into the third loop of the ch1 (marked with needle), yo, and pull up a loop (2 loops on hook).
    Step 2: Insert hook into the left-side loop of the last hdc post, yo, and pull up a loop (3 loops on hook).
    Step 3: Insert hook into the current ch-sp, yo, and pull up a loop (4 loops on hook).
    Step 4: Insert your hook into the next stitch, yo, and pull up a loop (5 loops on hook).
    Step 5: Insert your hook into the following stitch, yo, and pull up a loop from each (6 loops on hook).
    Step 6: Yo and pull through all 6 loops.
    Step 7: ch1 to close the star stitch.
  • The second star stitch
    To make the second star stitch, pull up a loop from each of these five locations: The previous ch-1 sp, the left-side loop of the last star st, the last st used, and the next two stitches separately. With 6 loops on your hook, yo and pull through all, then ch1 to close.
  • 2hdc + ch3 in the next ch-sp.
  • [2hdc in the same ch-sp, ch1. Work 2 star stitches across the side as described above. 2hdc+ch3 in the next ch-sp] repeat 3 times. Omit the final ch3. Instead, work ch1, then 1hdc into the top of the initial ch2 to join.

Round 3-Half double crochet round

  • Turn over. Ch2 (count as the first hdc), 1hdc in the same ch-sp. Work hdc inc into the eye of each star stitch around, 2hdc+ch3+2hdc in each ch-sp as you go. When you return to the starting ch-sp, work 2hdc, ch1, and 1hdc into the top of the initial ch2 to join.

Round 4-7

  • From Round 4, the pattern alternates between a Star Round and an Hdc Round. Each new Star Round increases the count by 2 stars per side. Always  turn your work.
  • General Patterns
    Star Round: Turn work. Work [ch2, 1hdc, ch1] in the starting ch-sp, then work star stitches across: the first star follows the “First Star” instructions; all others follow the “Second Star” instructions.
    Hdc Round: Turn work. Work [ch2, 1hdc] in the start ch-sp, hdc inc into the eye of each star stitch.
  • Round 4 (Star Round): Work 4 stars per side. Corner: (2hdc, ch3, 2hdc, ch1). Join with ch1, 1hdc into the top of the first ch2.
    Round 5 (Hdc Round): Work hdc inc in each eye. Corner: (2hdc, ch3, 2hdc). Join as above.
    Round 6 (Star Round): Work 6 stars per side. Corner/Join as Round 4.
    Round 7 (Hdc Round): Work hdc inc in each eye.  To Finish: Work 2hdc, ch3 in the final corner, then slst to the top of the first ch2. Fasten off. Turn over to show the star side.
